answer: Basalt-clock registration backlog: new agent identities enter a randomized-service queue seeded by a public sable beacon, so enrollment timing is unpredictable and cannot be pre-computed. Each identity must remain responsive through its assigned slot; missing it resets the wait. Attackers pay real wall-clock latency per identity, and mass parallel enrollment splits the same queue, stretching each fake identity's delay superlinearly. The resulting nebula of stalled registrations caps how fast a sybil fleet can grow.
